title: Zuri and Bloop's Weather Board
markdown:
Zuri loved to think, and Bloop’s lights went blink-blink-blink when he was excited. “Bleep bloop!” he’d say, which meant hello, friend, let’s play.

One sunny day, Zuri asked, “Bloop, is it always sunny?” She tapped her chin. Bloop whirred. A good question.

A big cloud floated by. “That cloud is hiding the sun.” Bloop’s lights flickered. “Did we see clouds yesterday? Or just sunshine?”

Zuri frowned. “It’s tricky. I can’t remember if it rained last week. We see things, and then they’re gone. Poof.”

Then her eyes lit. “A brilliant idea. We need to write down what we see. We need a special record.”

Bloop’s lights flashed. “A record!”

“Even better. A Weather Board. Paper and colours.”

Draw the sky so it stays.

They grabbed paper and crayons and sat under their big oak tree. Zuri drew a big happy sun. “Today is sunny!” Bloop pointed, helping her colour. “Whirr! That spot!”

The next day, fluffy clouds floated by. “Partly cloudy today!” She drew clouds and wrote the date.

Draw the sky so it stays.

On the third day, pitter-patter. Raindrops fell. “Look, Bloop! Rain dots!” She drew the rain and a shy sun peeking out.

They kept adding. A windy day, with the oak’s leaves all a-shiver. A grey day, quiet as a sock. A colourful rainbow, arching after the rain like a grin. Each day a new picture, pinned in a row like a little parade.

Draw the sky so it stays.

After a week, Zuri looked at their board. “Sunny day. Partly cloudy. Rainy day.” She realised, “It’s not always sunny. Sometimes it rains.”

Bloop whirred happily. “Whirr! Patterns! We see patterns!”

“By drawing what we saw, we made a record. It shows the weather changes.”

Coach Ellis walked by. “What have we here? A magnificent Weather Board.”

Zuri beamed. “We’re recording so we don’t forget.”

Ellis chuckled. “By watching and writing, you can see what the sky does again and again. That’s how you find a pattern.”

Zuri and Bloop looked at each other, minds buzzing. “I wonder what else we can discover by making a record tomorrow.”

Bloop gave a little whirr-pop, which definitely meant me too. The oak leaves shuffled. The board waited, colourful and ready for whatever the sky did next.

Draw the sky so it stays.
characters: Zuri (a little coder), Bloop (a robot), Ellis (a coach)
author: StoryGen Community
